fields.description: Whose availability this is. It is also the docname, and it is unique: a volunteer has one schedule, not one per year. A society that tried to keep several would have to decide which one a deployment asks, and there is no answer to that which is not a rule somebody has to remember.
fields.label: Volunteer

fields.description: Whether this person is willing to serve on a public holiday. Recorded because a society mounting a response over a holiday needs to know who it can ask without asking everybody. Nothing in this app reads a holiday calendar yet, so this is carried and shown rather than matched on; it is a fact a coordinator uses, not a filter the server applies.
fields.label: Available On Holidays

fields.description: The first day this pattern describes. Optional: a volunteer who has not said means the pattern holds from now on, which is what most people mean when they fill in a weekly availability grid. Where it is set, a deployment beginning before it is not matched against this schedule.
fields.label: Valid From

fields.description: The last day this pattern describes — a student free until term restarts, somebody available until they move. Optional, and empty means indefinitely. Refused if it falls before the start.
fields.label: Valid To

fields.description: Which windows on which days this volunteer is free. One row per day-and-slot pair, so a person free on Saturday mornings and all day Sunday has three rows rather than a sentence somebody has to read. Deliberately a *pattern* rather than a list of dates: a volunteer fills this in once, and a schedule expanded into a dated row per day for a year would be tens of thousands of rows that go stale the moment somebody's Tuesdays change.
fields.label: Available Days

fields.description: Anything about when this person can serve that the pattern cannot say. Never read by code.
fields.label: Notes
